questions.text:
Let p,q, r, s represent the following propositions.

p: x[latex]\in[/latex]{8,9,10,11,12}
q: x is a composite number
r: x is a perfect square
s: x is a prime number

The integer x[latex]\geq[/latex]2 which satisfies [latex]\neg((p\Rightarrow q)\wedge (\neg r \vee \neg s))[/latex] is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex] eg((p\Rightarrow q)\wedge( eg r\vee eg s))\equiv(p\wedge eg q)\vee(r\wedge s)[/latex]

- [latex]r\wedge s[/latex] (perfect square and prime) is impossible.
- So we need [latex]p\wedge eg q[/latex]: x in {8, 9, 10, 11, 12} and not composite. Only 11 qualifies.

Answer: 11

questions.text: Let [latex]a_{n}[/latex] be the number of n-bit strings that do NOT contain two consecutive 1s. Which one of the following is the recurrence relation for [latex]a_{n}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Look at the first bit of a valid n-bit string:
- starts with 0: the rest is any valid (n [latex]-[/latex] 1)-bit string [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_{n-1}[/latex]
- starts with 1: the next bit must be 0, then any valid (n [latex]-[/latex] 2)-bit string [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_{n-2}[/latex]

[latex]a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}[/latex]

questions.text:
A probability density function on the interval [a,1] is given by 1/[latex]x^{2}[/latex]
 and outside this interval the value of the function is zero.The value of a is __________.
questions.solution:
Total probability must be 1:
[latex]\int_a^1\frac{1}{x^2}dx=\left[-\frac1x\right]_a^1=\frac1a-1=1\Rightarrow a=\frac12[/latex]

Answer: 0.5

questions.text: Two eigen values of a 3x3 real matrix P are (2+[latex]\sqrt{-1}[/latex]) and 3.The determinantof P is __________.
questions.solution:
A real matrix has complex eigenvalues in conjugate pairs, so [latex]2-i[/latex] is the third eigenvalue.

[latex]\det P=(2+i)(2-i)\times3=(4+1)\times3=15[/latex]

Answer: 15
